newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures open mixed as marks slide.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures open mixed as marks slide.

text.p: IMM currency futures opened mixed on Tuesday with December mark futures hitting another pit-trading contract low in early activity of 0.6392, after making an all-time low on GLOBEX overnight of 0.6364.
Traders and analysts said the overall mark trend looked bearish, despite a modest pullback overnight in the dollar's rally against the Continental currencies.

"The way things feel right at this point, I don't see why the dollar would want to fall back very sharply, as long as you continue to stay below 0.6428 on the December D-mark," said one currency analyst on the trading floor.
He said he is targeting 0.6354 as an initial downward objective for the December mark, with a possible bottom of 0.6322. One technical analyst said he saw December mark support at 0.6317.

December Swiss francs and December sterling declined, as well, in early trading. Traders said the dollar continued to firm on the growing notion that it offers safe harbor during the run-up to European monetary unification.
U.S. economic data being released Tuesday on retail sales and new home sales was seen as having little impact on currency futures trading, traders said.
December yen rebounded modestly Tuesday partly on cash crosses from a contract low set Monday of $0.008725.
"We've got an inside day working today and I think that will probably hold true," a technical analyst said.
Monday's December yen high of $0.008825 may cap upside potential Tuesday, but the technical analyst said he is focusing on selling strategies.
"We'll look ultimately for a retest of the $0.008725 low from yesterday and then continue on down," he said.

At 0922 CST/1522 GMT, December yen were up $0.000064 to $0.008801, marks were off $0.0034 to $0.6396, Swiss francs were off $0.0033 to $0.7527, sterling were off $0.0218 to $1.6560, Canadian dollars were up $0.0007 to $0.7421, Australian dollars were off $0.0197 to $0.7984 and Mexican pesos were off $0.000075 at $0.125800.
